messages:
maya: Heads up — onboarding Arcadia's LoRA (arcadia-lora-v2) into rwd-base-30b-int4 failed our quickpack. Seeing tokenizer mismatches + JSON-extract exact-match drop. anyone seen this pattern?
sam: can you paste the quickpack summary / command you ran?
maya: ran: `./run_quick_eval --model rwd-base-30b-int4 --adapter arcadia-lora-v2 --evalset arcadia_qp.json --out results.json --batch 8`
maya: jq output: `{"json_extract_em": 0.61, "f1": 0.73}` — baseline float16 run earlier was `{"json_extract_em": 0.78, "f1": 0.75}`
eval-bot: QuickPack run complete — results uploaded to gs://redwood-evals/arcadia/3612349999/results.json :white_check_mark:
nina: EM drop from 0.78 -> 0.61 is large. is this reproducing only on int4?
maya: yes — I re-ran adapter on rwd-base-30b-fp16 (no quant) and EM is 0.76. so adapter itself looks ok. quant path seems to expose something.
lucas: two usual suspects: tokenizer id mapping or quantized kernel mismatch. any token id diffs between training tokenizer and production tokeniser?
maya: ran token map diff script: `python tools/token_map_diff.py --base rwd-base-30b --adapter-tokenizer arcadia-tokenizer.json`
maya: found 2 remapped tokens: `\u2019` (apostrophe variant) and `<ARC_CUST>` (custom tag) — IDs differ by 1 and 3 respectively.
toni: also check long-context behavior — int4 can mis-handle padding/KV reuse when sequence > 512. any pattern with longer prompts?
maya: yes failing examples skew long. short prompts (<128) are fine. long ones (>512) show extra truncation or unexpected commas in numeric fields.
sam: can you paste one failing example (prompt, gold JSON, model output)?
maya: sure:
```
PROMPT: Please extract invoice fields for the following document: <long invoice text ...>
GOLD: {"invoice_number":"INV-2034","invoice_total":"1000.00","vendor":"Acme"}
OUTPUT (int4): {"invoice_number":"INV-2034","invoice_total":"1,000.00","vendor":"Acme"}
```
maya: note the comma inserted in invoice_total only in int4 path.
lucas: that smells like tokenizer normalization / byte pair segmentation difference — comma inserted because token boundary differs, then post-processing formatting step mis-applies.
nina: action plan: 1) run 1k-sample quickpack on fp16/fp32 to confirm delta, 2) run token-id remap patch (map adapter tokens to base ids) and re-eval on int4, 3) try int8 fallback to see if issue is quant level specific.
maya: I'll run token remap + int8 quickpack tonight and drop results.
sam: I'll add `--debug-token-ids` instrumentation to the quickpack runner to log token ids and the tokenized strings for failing examples; will store as `debug_token_ids.jsonl`.
eval-bot: scheduled debug quickpack job for arcadia: job_id=arcadia-debug-3612350400, runtime target=linux-gpu-rt3
toni: if token remap fixes it, we should add a small token-id-check to our onboarding checklist to catch this earlier. :memo:
maya: agreed. also suspect KV-cache alignment — i'll try `--skip_kv_cache` once as a quick probe.
sam: added the flag and log hook, will kick when maya pushes remap patch.
maya: pushing patch now, will report back after the run. thanks all.
